text:
ravi (Acme): Hey, heads up — after our SSO-driven API key rotation this morning some of our backend instances started getting 401 invalid_api_key when calling Redwood's embeddings endpoint. It looks intermittent: some requests succeed, others 401.

ravi (Acme): Example repro from one of our services (node):

```
// service makes requests every 30s
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'x-api-key': process.env.REDWOOD_KEY },
  body: JSON.stringify({ input: 'hello' })
})
```

ravi (Acme): After ~15 minutes the same instance starts failing with 401. We think the key TTL from our SSO/Vault is 15m.

maya (Support): Thanks for the details — sorry you're hitting that. Two quick Qs: 1) are the failing requests returning any Redwood headers (x-request-id, x-retry) in the 401 response? 2) can you paste the exact header shape (mask keys) you set in the requests (Authorization vs x-api-key)?

ravi (Acme): 1) 401 response includes `x-request-id: req_3f2b` and no x-retry. 2) we use `x-api-key`. Example header (masked): `x-api-key: red_*****************`

elena (SRE): Quick hypothesis: your rotation issues look like a client-side credential cache problem. If Vault/SAML issues short-lived keys, the running process may still hold the old value in env memory and never pick up the rotated secret. That would make failures start after the old key expires.

ravi (Acme): That makes sense. But why do some requests still succeed on the same instance?

maya (Support): Two possibilities: 1) you have multiple worker processes where some were restarted and loaded the new key while others still use the old key; 2) you have a per-request in-memory cache of the header and some code paths bypass the refreshed loader.

jay (Eng): Another thing to check: are you using a Secrets Manager client that auto-refreshes tokens (and are you actually calling its getSecret when making requests)? If you cache the secret at startup into process.env and never re-read, rotate will break until restart.

ravi (Acme): We do set process.env.REDWOOD_KEY at startup from Secrets Manager and rely on a separate cron to write the new secret to the host env file. We don't restart processes automatically.

maya (Support): Repro steps that will confirm this quickly: 1) on a single instance, call the embeddings endpoint repeatedly and note 200 then 401 after TTL. 2) rotate the key in your SSO/Vault and then restart the node process — if restarts immediately fix the 401s, it's definitely a local cache/refresh issue.

elena (SRE): Additional quick test: tail your service logs and run `env | grep REDWOOD` before and after rotation to see if the running env actually gets updated. Also send a manual curl with the new key from that host to isolate whether Redwood accepts the new key. Example curl we use for checks: 

```
curl -i -H "x-api-key: red_newkeyMASKED" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

ravi (Acme): Ran those: manual curl with the new key from the host -> 200. The running service requests still 401 until we restart the process.

maya (Support): That nails it — the instance has the new key in the host but the service still uses an old in-memory secret. Fixes: - make your secret fetcher call Secrets Manager per request or on a short timer (e.g., re-read every 60s) - or write the refreshed secret to a file and signal the process to reload config (SIGHUP) - or use a sidecar that injects refreshed header at request-time.

jay (Eng): For short-term mitigation you can also extend the TTL in Vault to reduce rotation frequency while you deploy a refresh path. But long-term prefer credential refresh in the client or use our SDK which supports short-lived credentials refresh patterns.

ravi (Acme): Thanks — we'll implement an in-process refresh loop. One more question: will Redwood surface a different error for scope mismatch vs expired key? We want to detect expired keys separately in our monitoring.

maya (Support): Good question. Expired/invalid keys will return 401 invalid_api_key. Scope-mismatch (e.g., embeddings-only key used for generation) also returns 401 but payload often contains `allowed_scopes` in the body when available. We recommend checking the response body for those fields and logging x-request-id for support traces.

devops-bot: Ticket #INC-7832 created for this thread and linked to support case SC-4591 :ticket:

ravi (Acme): Resolving for now — rotating to a refreshable client and adding an alert when 401 rate > 5%/5m. Will follow up if it recurs. Thanks for triage! :pray:

maya (Support): Great — ping us with the x-request-id if it comes back and we can pull server logs. Closing from support side pending confirmation. :thumbsup:
